products.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration
products.source:
* You can connect to Automation Cloud without routing traffic over the public internet using Azure Private Link, with primary and secondary gateways providing built-in continuity during regional outages.
* SCIM User Sync, available in preview for Enterprise plans, automates user lifecycle management by synchronizing user creation, updates, and deprovisioning directly from Microsoft Entra ID or Okta.
* Relay client 26.4.2 lets you connect the persistent tunnel through `cloud.uipath.com:443`. This release also adds the `relay describe <id>` and `relay list` commands for inspecting relay information, and introduces log management controls.
* AI Trust Layer PII in-flight masking adds support for four Nordic identity entities: Norway Identity Number, Finland National ID, Sweden National ID, and Danish Identity Number.
* You can power UI Automation Semantic activities with your own large language model subscription instead of the UiPath-managed subscription.
* Updating the UI Automation Activities package changes the default model for Semantic activities (excluding Close Popup) to PathMini.

analysis.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration
analysis.summary: This release adds private connectivity, preview SCIM user synchronization, Relay client 26.4.2 enhancements, expanded AI Trust Layer PII masking, custom LLM subscription support for UI Automation Semantic activities, and a default model update to PathMini for most Semantic activities.
analysis.overall_analysis: The changes focus on enterprise connectivity, identity lifecycle automation, governance, and flexibility in AI-powered automation. They also update the default AI model behavior in UI Automation Semantic activities, which may affect how those activities perform after package updates.

products.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration
products.source:
* The South Korea global cloud region is now generally available, with full data residency for most platform services.
* Data Fabric is now available in the South Korea region.
* Data Export is now available in the Admin Portal. Organization administrators can configure and monitor exports of platform data — Orchestrator events, audit logs, Maestro traces, and agent traces — to destinations such as Azure Event Hub, AWS SQS, Databricks, Arize, and OpenTelemetry collectors.
* New License Viewer and License Administrator roles let Org Admins delegate license management without granting full Org Admin access.
* PII in-flight masking now extends to files that agents download at runtime and pass to LLMs as multi-modal inputs.
* The Relay client can now run as a container image using Podman or Kubernetes, and Relay is now available in the United States delayed and European Union delayed regions.
* UiPath is unifying outbound IP ranges across Automation Cloud and Test Cloud services into a single regional set. The transition window begins June 16, 2026, and legacy service-specific ranges are phased out starting September 16, 2026.
* Creating a trial organization with a social sign-in now requires a business email.
* Test Cloud now includes two new built-in user groups, App Test Developer and Tester, optimized for testing scenarios.

It adds new roles, data export options, relay deployment choices, testing-focused groups, and updates to outbound IP management and trial sign-up requirements.

changes.summary: General improvements and bug fixes were made to enhance platform stability and performance.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces defects and improves the consistency and responsiveness of the administration experience, but the exact areas affected are not stated.
changes.impact: Administrators using Automation Cloud Dedicated Administration and Test Cloud Dedicated Administration.

products.name: Orchestrator
products.source:
* New credential store integration: Delinea Secret Server (read-only), the successor to Thycotic Secret Server.

* Automatic cleanup of Default Execution Identity references.

analysis.name: Orchestrator
analysis.summary: Orchestrator adds a new Delinea Secret Server credential store integration, more detailed queue item JSON schema validation errors, automatic cleanup of Default Execution Identity references, Personal Workspace subfolder management permissions, and tenant-level resources support in binding overwrites.
analysis.overall_analysis: These changes strengthen integration options, improve diagnostics and administration, and expand permission and resource configuration capabilities. The release is likely significant for administrators and developers managing credentials, queues, workspace permissions, execution identities, and resource bindings.

changes.name: Delinea Secret Server credential store integration
changes.summary: A new credential store integration was added for Delinea Secret Server in read-only mode, identified as the successor to Thycotic Secret Server.
changes.analysis: This expands supported secret-management integrations and may help organizations align with Delinea branding or platform transitions from Thycotic Secret Server. The read-only limitation is important for implementation planning.
changes.impact: Administrators and security teams integrating Orchestrator with external credential stores, especially organizations using or migrating to Delinea Secret Server.

changes.name: Detailed queue item JSON schema validation errors
changes.summary: Queue item endpoints now provide detailed JSON schema validation errors.
changes.analysis: More detailed validation feedback should make API troubleshooting faster and reduce time spent diagnosing malformed payloads when interacting with queue item endpoints.
changes.impact: Developers and integrators using Orchestrator queue item endpoints.

changes.name: Automatic cleanup of Default Execution Identity references
changes.summary: Default Execution Identity references are now cleaned up automatically.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces stale or invalid references and lowers administrative overhead, improving configuration hygiene and possibly preventing issues caused by lingering identity references.
changes.impact: Administrators managing execution identities and related Orchestrator configurations.

changes.name: Subfolder management permissions in Personal Workspace
changes.summary: Subfolder management permissions were added in Personal Workspace.
changes.analysis: This enhances access control granularity within Personal Workspace, allowing better management of who can organize or administer subfolders.
changes.impact: Users and administrators working with Personal Workspace permissions and folder structures.

changes.name: Tenant-level resources support in binding overwrites
changes.summary: Binding overwrites now support tenant-level resources.
changes.analysis: This broadens how resource bindings can be configured and reused across a tenant, which may simplify multi-scope deployments and centralized resource management.
changes.impact: Administrators and developers configuring bindings and tenant-level resources.

products.name: Agents

analysis.name: Agents
analysis.summary: Agents introduces a new Prompt editor with rich text editing, `@`-triggered insertion of inline references, Markdown formatting, and automatic rename propagation.
analysis.overall_analysis: This is a usability-focused enhancement that likely streamlines prompt authoring and maintenance for agent builders. It should improve editing efficiency, clarity, and consistency when working with prompts that reference arguments, tools, contexts, escalations, and outputs.

changes.name: New Prompt editor
changes.summary: A new Prompt editor provides a rich text editing experience, allowing input arguments, tools, contexts, escalations, and outputs to be inserted as color-coded inline references using a single `@` trigger, and also includes Markdown formatting and automatic rename propagation.
changes.analysis: The editor likely makes prompt creation more intuitive and less error-prone by improving discoverability of insertable elements, visual clarity of references, and consistency when referenced items are renamed.
changes.impact: Users authoring and maintaining prompts in Agents.

products.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration

Automation Cloud Administration and Test.summary: This release adds private connectivity, preview SCIM user synchronization, Relay client 26.4.2 enhancements, expanded AI Trust Layer PII masking, custom LLM subscription support for UI Automation Semantic activities, and a default model update to PathMini for most Semantic activities.
Automation Cloud Administration and Test.overall_analysis: The changes focus on enterprise connectivity, identity lifecycle automation, governance, and flexibility in AI-powered automation. They also update the default AI model behavior in UI Automation Semantic activities, which may affect how those activities perform after package updates.

changes.name: Azure Private Link support
changes.summary: You can connect to Automation Cloud using Azure Private Link without routing traffic over the public internet. Primary and secondary gateways provide built-in continuity during regional outages.
changes.analysis: This likely improves network security posture and resilience for organizations that need private connectivity and continuity planning.
changes.impact: Organizations using Automation Cloud, especially enterprise environments with strict networking and availability requirements.

changes.name: SCIM User Sync preview
changes.summary: SCIM User Sync is available in preview for Enterprise plans and automates user lifecycle management by synchronizing user creation, updates, and deprovisioning from Microsoft Entra ID or Okta.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces manual identity administration and helps keep access data aligned with identity providers.
changes.impact: Enterprise plan customers using Microsoft Entra ID or Okta for identity management.

changes.name: Relay client 26.4.2 enhancements
changes.summary: Relay client 26.4.2 allows the persistent tunnel to connect through `cloud.uipath.com:443`, adds the `relay describe <id>` and `relay list` commands for inspecting relay information, and introduces log management controls.
changes.analysis: These updates likely simplify connectivity and operational troubleshooting while improving manageability of relay deployments.
changes.impact: Users and administrators operating Relay client connections and persistent tunnels.

changes.name: Nordic identity entity support for PII masking
changes.summary: AI Trust Layer PII in-flight masking now supports Norway Identity Number, Finland National ID, Sweden National ID, and Danish Identity Number.
changes.analysis: This expands data protection coverage for additional regional identity formats.
changes.impact: Organizations processing Nordic personal identity data through AI Trust Layer.

changes.name: Custom LLM subscription support for Semantic activities
changes.summary: UI Automation Semantic activities can now be powered by your own large language model subscription instead of the UiPath-managed subscription.
changes.analysis: This likely gives customers more control over model sourcing, billing, and governance for AI-backed UI automation.
changes.impact: Users of UI Automation Semantic activities who want to use their own LLM subscription.

changes.name: Default Semantic model changed to PathMini
changes.summary: Updating the UI Automation Activities package changes the default model for Semantic activities, excluding Close Popup, to PathMini.
changes.analysis: This may alter default runtime behavior or results for Semantic activities after package updates because the underlying model selection changes automatically.
changes.impact: Users who update the UI Automation Activities package and rely on default model settings for Semantic activities.

Action Center.summary: Action Center now supports using a Coded Action App as the task interface for tasks created by agents, RPA processes, and Maestro processes.
Action Center.overall_analysis: This extends task UI flexibility by allowing code-first interfaces across multiple task-producing automation types.

changes.name: Coded Action App task interface support
changes.summary: You can use a Coded Action App as the interface for Action Center tasks created by agents, RPA processes, and Maestro processes.
changes.analysis: This likely enables more customizable and developer-driven task experiences in Action Center.
changes.impact: Developers and users working with Action Center tasks from agents, RPA processes, and Maestro processes.

Agents.summary: Agents gains a new Premium model tier in preview with Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 for advanced reasoning, multi-step planning, and extended context handling.
Agents.overall_analysis: This expands the available model options for higher-capability agent scenarios, particularly where more complex reasoning and planning are needed.

changes.name: Premium model tier preview
changes.summary: A new Premium model tier introduces Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 for agents, available in preview, with support for advanced reasoning, multi-step planning, and extended context handling.
changes.analysis: This likely improves the sophistication of agent behaviors for more demanding use cases.
changes.impact: Users building or running agents that benefit from stronger reasoning and larger-context model capabilities.

Apps.summary: Apps now lets you create and manage Coded Action Apps, which are custom code-first applications built with the UiPath Coded Action App SDK and UiPath TypeScript SDK for use in Action Center.
Apps.overall_analysis: This adds a developer-centric application model that integrates with Action Center task experiences.

changes.name: Create and manage Coded Action Apps
changes.summary: You can create and manage Coded Action Apps, which are custom code-first applications built in your IDE using the UiPath Coded Action App SDK and UiPath TypeScript SDK, for use as the task interface in Action Center.
changes.analysis: This likely broadens extensibility and enables teams to build tailored task interfaces using code-based tooling.
changes.impact: Developers building custom Action Center task interfaces.

Automation Ops.summary: Automation Ops adds AI Trust Layer controls for UiPath-managed models and a Studio Web policy setting to cap agent iterations before workflow publication.
Automation Ops.overall_analysis: These updates strengthen governance over model availability and agent design-time behavior.

changes.name: Model availability controls in AI Trust Layer policy
changes.summary: From the AI Trust Layer policy, you can enable or disable specific UiPath-managed models at the provider or individual model level on a per-product basis, and control whether newly released models become automatically available.
changes.analysis: This likely helps organizations govern AI model exposure and rollout more precisely across products.
changes.impact: Administrators managing AI Trust Layer policy and model governance across UiPath products.

changes.name: Agent iteration cap in Studio Web policy
changes.summary: From the Studio Web policy, you can cap the number of iterations an agent runs before a workflow is published.
changes.analysis: This likely helps prevent runaway loops and adds design-time safeguards for agent behavior.
changes.impact: Administrators governing Studio Web and users publishing workflows with agents.

Healing Agent.summary: Healing Agent now exposes failure reasons through Robot logs in Orchestrator.
Healing Agent.overall_analysis: This improves troubleshooting visibility when healing attempts fail.

changes.name: Failure reason visibility in Robot logs
changes.summary: You can see the reason why Healing Agent has failed by navigating to Robot logs in Orchestrator.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces diagnostic effort by surfacing failure details in an existing operational log location.
changes.impact: Users and operators troubleshooting Healing Agent failures in Orchestrator.

Industry & Department Solutions.summary: Supply Chain and Retail solutions now allow optional standard-schema columns in ingest payloads, and the Data Quality Dashboard has been rebuilt into a single scrolling overview with multiple KPI, trend, breakdown, and drill-down views.
Industry & Department Solutions.overall_analysis: The updates improve flexibility for data ingestion and expand data quality visibility through a more consolidated dashboard experience.

changes.name: Optional standard-schema columns in Supply Chain and Retail
changes.summary: In Supply Chain and Retail solutions, you can declare standard-schema columns as optional, allowing non-required fields to be omitted from ingest payloads. Omitted fields are stored as NULL or their default value.
changes.analysis: This likely simplifies integrations where some standard fields are not always available while preserving schema handling.
changes.impact: Users integrating data into Supply Chain and Retail solutions.

changes.name: Rebuilt Data Quality Dashboard
changes.summary: The Data Quality Dashboard is rebuilt as a single scrolling overview with a Current health snapshot of five KPI cards, three trend charts, a ranked Top error codes table, searchable Breakdown by table and Breakdown by request views, and a table-level drill-down scoped to a selected table, solution, and date range.
changes.analysis: This likely makes data quality monitoring more centralized and actionable by combining high-level status with drill-down analysis.
changes.impact: Users monitoring data quality across solutions and requests.

Maestro.summary: Maestro introduces Maestro Case, a new preview Function Service Task type, and canvas usability enhancements for process design.
Maestro.overall_analysis: These changes expand Maestro into case-oriented orchestration, add deterministic Python function execution from processes, and streamline process modeling.

changes.name: Maestro Case project type
changes.summary: Maestro Case is a new project type for goal-driven work where AI agents and rules can move cases forward automatically and humans step in when judgment or policy requires it. It includes a Case Plan Designer, Case Manager, Case App, and Case Instance Management.
changes.analysis: This likely broadens Maestro from process orchestration into case management scenarios that combine automation and human decision points.
changes.impact: Teams designing and operating goal-driven case workflows involving agents, rules, and human intervention.

changes.name: Start and wait for Function Service Task preview
changes.summary: A new Start and wait for Function Service Task type lets you run deterministic Python logic published with the `uip` CLI directly from a process, with inputs and outputs mapped automatically from the function's schema. It is available in preview.
changes.analysis: This likely improves integration of deterministic code execution into processes while reducing manual mapping effort.
changes.impact: Process designers who want to invoke Python logic from Maestro processes.

changes.name: Canvas authoring enhancements
changes.summary: The canvas now includes an element toolbar with boundary event and marker buttons, a quick add menu for placing nodes directly on the canvas with pre-associated automation types, and a Properties panel that automatically opens the implementation area for unconfigured elements.
changes.analysis: These changes likely speed up modeling and reduce friction when configuring process elements.
changes.impact: Users designing processes in the Maestro canvas.

Orchestrator.summary: Orchestrator adds inline chip filters to Processes Registry and Resources, updates Maestro process type labels, and refreshes create and edit forms with a card-based layout and sticky breadcrumb bar.
Orchestrator.overall_analysis: The release improves usability and aligns terminology with Maestro naming updates across the platform.

changes.name: Inline chip filters for grid columns
changes.summary: The Processes Registry and Resources pages now add inline chip filters for fixed-value columns, allowing one-click filtering without expanding a dropdown.
changes.analysis: This likely makes grid filtering faster and more convenient for common fixed-value fields.
changes.impact: Users working with the Processes Registry and Resources pages in Orchestrator.

changes.name: Updated Maestro process type labels
changes.summary: Orchestrator updates Maestro process type labels throughout the product: Agentic process becomes Maestro BPMN, Case Management becomes Maestro Case, and Flow becomes Maestro Flow.
changes.analysis: This aligns Orchestrator terminology with the latest Maestro naming conventions.
changes.impact: All Orchestrator users who view or manage Maestro-related process types.

changes.name: Create and edit form redesign
changes.summary: Create and edit forms across Orchestrator now use a card layout with shadow and rounded corners, consistent spacing, and a sticky breadcrumb bar that remains visible while scrolling.
changes.analysis: This likely improves navigation and visual consistency during form-based workflows.
changes.impact: Users creating or editing items across Orchestrator.

Solutions.summary: Solutions now allows unlinking resources during version change configuration so they can be recreated in the solution folder at upgrade time or linked to a different existing component.
Solutions.overall_analysis: This adds more flexibility to resource management during upgrades and version transitions.

changes.name: Unlink resources during version change configuration
changes.summary: When configuring a version change in the resource explorer, you can unlink resources previously linked to an existing component, then either let them be created fresh in the solution folder at upgrade time or link them to a different existing component.
changes.analysis: This likely helps administrators handle dependency and resource mapping changes more cleanly during upgrades.
changes.impact: Users managing version changes and resources in Solutions.

Studio Web.summary: Studio Web updates project type names, reorganizes project creation by category, adds local run support for RPA workflows, improves debugging and resource mapping awareness, and shows progress feedback when duplicating projects.
Studio Web.overall_analysis: The release refines naming consistency, project creation experience, and developer workflow efficiency in Studio Web.

changes.name: Updated project type names
changes.summary: Studio Web updates project type names: Agentic process becomes Maestro BPMN, API Automation becomes API function, and Automations becomes RPA workflow.
changes.analysis: This aligns Studio Web terminology with updated product and feature naming across the platform.
changes.impact: Studio Web users creating or managing projects.

changes.name: Project creation organized by category
changes.summary: The project creation view is now organized by category. The New project dropdown, Start building modal, and Add project to solution context menu group project types under Business orchestration, Task automation, and Building blocks.
changes.analysis: This likely makes project discovery and selection easier by grouping options into clearer categories.
changes.impact: Users creating projects in Studio Web.

changes.name: Local run for RPA workflows and debugger behavior update
changes.summary: You can now run an RPA workflow locally from Studio Web without publishing it first. The debugger no longer pauses on handled exceptions caught by Retry Scope or Try Catch activities.
changes.analysis: This likely speeds up development and reduces unnecessary debugger interruptions during expected exception handling.
changes.impact: Developers building and debugging RPA workflows in Studio Web.

changes.name: Resource definition mismatch warning
changes.summary: Activities now show a warning hint when their bound resource has a different definition at debug time than it had at design time. The hint includes a direct link to update the resource mapping.
changes.analysis: This likely helps users identify and correct resource drift that could affect debugging outcomes.
changes.impact: Studio Web users debugging projects with bound resources.

changes.name: Project duplication progress toast
changes.summary: When you duplicate a project, Studio Web shows a toast notification confirming that duplication is in progress.
changes.analysis: This provides clearer feedback for an asynchronous operation and may reduce uncertainty during project duplication.
changes.impact: Users duplicating projects in Studio Web.

Test Manager.summary: Test Manager adds TMH-based Project Configuration export/import, group sorting in Test Cloud structured views, Romanian system prompt support in Autopilot, and multiple Performance Testing improvements including retry-aware reporting, Workflow Analyzer, and Live Streaming.
Test Manager.overall_analysis: The release expands portability and administration capabilities while significantly improving performance testing diagnostics and observability.

changes.name: Project Configuration export and import via TMH
changes.summary: You can export and import Project Configuration as part of TMH files, including custom field definitions, user authorizations, roles, reporting time zone, automation context folder, and governance settings.
changes.analysis: This likely simplifies migration, backup, or replication of Test Manager project configuration across environments.
changes.impact: Test Manager administrators managing project setup and portability.

changes.name: Group sorting in structured views on Test Cloud
changes.summary: You can sort groups ascending or descending in custom structured views when using Test Manager via Test Cloud.
changes.analysis: This likely improves usability when navigating grouped test data.
changes.impact: Test Cloud users working with custom structured views in Test Manager.

changes.name: Romanian language support for Autopilot system prompts
changes.summary: Autopilot now supports Romanian for system prompts.
changes.analysis: This expands language support for users working in Romanian.
changes.impact: Autopilot users in Test Manager who need Romanian system prompt support.

changes.name: Retry-aware Performance Testing reporting
changes.summary: Performance Testing reporting now differentiates expected retry behavior from genuine execution failures, so retries that ultimately succeed no longer inflate error counts or appear as errors in charts.
changes.analysis: This likely makes reports more accurate and reduces false signals in error metrics.
changes.impact: Users reviewing Performance Testing results and charts.

changes.name: Workflow Analyzer for Performance Testing
changes.summary: A new Workflow Analyzer in Performance Testing automatically scans test automation projects during dry runs to identify selectors, interaction modes, and workflow patterns that are incompatible with or unlikely to scale in performance testing.
changes.analysis: This likely helps teams detect scalability and compatibility issues earlier in the testing cycle.
changes.impact: Users preparing or validating test automation projects for performance testing.

changes.name: Live Streaming for Performance Testing
changes.summary: Live Streaming for Performance Testing lets you open a real-time view of test execution directly from an active dry run to identify issues earlier.
changes.analysis: This likely improves real-time troubleshooting and visibility during test execution.
changes.impact: Users monitoring active performance testing dry runs.

products.name: Automation Cloud Administration and Test Cloud Administration

Automation Cloud Administration and Test.summary: This release expands regional availability, administration capabilities, and governance controls for Automation Cloud and Test Cloud administration. It adds new roles, data export options, relay deployment choices, testing-focused groups, and updates to outbound IP management and trial sign-up requirements.
Automation Cloud Administration and Test.overall_analysis: The changes emphasize enterprise administration, regional expansion, delegated governance, and operational control. They likely help organizations meet data residency, compliance, integration, and access management needs while preparing for upcoming networking changes.

changes.name: South Korea global cloud region generally available
changes.summary: The South Korea global cloud region is now generally available, with full data residency for most platform services.
changes.analysis: This likely supports customers that need production use in South Korea and require local data residency for compliance or operational reasons.
changes.impact: Organizations deploying in South Korea and teams with regional data residency requirements are affected.

changes.name: Data Fabric available in South Korea region
changes.summary: Data Fabric is now available in the South Korea region.
changes.analysis: This expands service availability in the region so customers can use Data Fabric without relying on another geography.
changes.impact: Customers using or planning to use Data Fabric in South Korea are affected.

changes.name: Data Export available in Admin Portal
changes.summary: Data Export is now available in the Admin Portal, allowing organization administrators to configure and monitor exports of platform data such as Orchestrator events, audit logs, Maestro traces, and agent traces to destinations including Azure Event Hub, AWS SQS, Databricks, Arize, and OpenTelemetry collectors.
changes.analysis: This likely improves observability, governance, and external analytics integration by centralizing export configuration for platform telemetry and audit data.
changes.impact: Organization administrators, compliance teams, and teams integrating UiPath platform data with external monitoring or analytics systems are affected.

changes.name: New License Viewer and License Administrator roles
changes.summary: New License Viewer and License Administrator roles allow Org Admins to delegate license management without granting full Org Admin access.
changes.analysis: This supports more granular access control and separation of duties for license administration.
changes.impact: Organization administrators and users responsible for license management are affected.

changes.name: PII in-flight masking extended to downloaded files
changes.summary: PII in-flight masking now also applies to files that agents download at runtime and pass to LLMs as multi-modal inputs.
changes.analysis: This likely strengthens privacy controls for agent workflows that process file-based content with LLMs.
changes.impact: Organizations using agents with LLMs, especially those handling sensitive data in files, are affected.

changes.name: Relay container image support and delayed region availability
changes.summary: The Relay client can now run as a container image using Podman or Kubernetes, and Relay is now available in the United States delayed and European Union delayed regions.
changes.analysis: This improves deployment flexibility for Relay and expands availability for customers operating in delayed regions.
changes.impact: Infrastructure teams deploying Relay and customers in United States delayed or European Union delayed regions are affected.

changes.name: Unified outbound IP ranges transition
changes.summary: UiPath is unifying outbound IP ranges across Automation Cloud and Test Cloud services into a single regional set. The transition window begins June 16, 2026, and legacy service-specific ranges are phased out starting September 16, 2026.
changes.analysis: This simplifies network allowlisting over time, but it also requires customers to plan updates before legacy ranges are phased out.
changes.impact: Network administrators and security teams maintaining allowlists for Automation Cloud and Test Cloud services are affected.

changes.name: Trial organizations with social sign-in require business email
changes.summary: Creating a trial organization with a social sign-in now requires a business email.
changes.analysis: This likely aims to improve account quality, enterprise alignment, or fraud prevention for trial sign-ups.
changes.impact: Prospective trial users who sign up with social sign-in are affected.

changes.name: New built-in Test Cloud user groups
changes.summary: Test Cloud now includes two new built-in user groups, App Test Developer and Tester, optimized for testing scenarios.
changes.analysis: This likely simplifies user provisioning and role assignment for testing-focused teams.
changes.impact: Test Cloud administrators and testing teams are affected.

Agents.summary: Agents receives upgrades for model availability, privacy protection, and authoring experience. The release adds new premium LLM models, extends PII masking to downloaded files used as multi-modal inputs, and introduces a richer Prompt editor.
Agents.overall_analysis: These changes strengthen both agent capability and governance. They likely help teams build more powerful agent experiences while improving usability and reducing privacy risk in LLM interactions.

changes.name: New premium LLM models available
changes.summary: Premium LLM models Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 are now available for workloads that require advanced reasoning, multi-step planning, and extended context handling.
changes.analysis: This expands model choice for demanding agent scenarios and may improve quality for complex reasoning tasks.
changes.impact: Teams building or running agents that need advanced reasoning, planning, or long-context processing are affected.

changes.name: PII in-flight masking for downloaded files
changes.summary: PII in-flight masking now extends to files that agents download at runtime and pass to LLMs as multi-modal inputs.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces the risk of exposing sensitive information in file-based LLM interactions.
changes.impact: Organizations using agents with file inputs and LLM integrations are affected.

changes.name: New Prompt editor
changes.summary: A new Prompt editor provides rich text editing, with input arguments, tools, contexts, escalations, and outputs inserted as color-coded inline references using a single `@` trigger, plus Markdown formatting and automatic rename propagation.
changes.analysis: This likely improves prompt authoring productivity, readability, and maintainability, especially in more complex agent configurations.
changes.impact: Users authoring and maintaining agent prompts are affected.

Automation Ops.summary: Automation Ops adds new AI Trust Layer controls for MCP onboarding, regional LLM routing, and configurable PII masking scope. The updates focus on governance and policy-based control for AI usage.
Automation Ops.overall_analysis: The release strengthens enterprise policy enforcement for AI scenarios. It likely helps organizations manage compliance, deployment geography, and privacy controls more precisely.

changes.name: MCP Dynamic Client Registration in AI Trust Layer policy
changes.summary: MCP Dynamic Client Registration can now be enabled within an AI Trust Layer policy to simplify onboarding and lifecycle management for MCP clients.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces administrative overhead and standardizes how MCP clients are introduced and managed under policy controls.
changes.impact: Administrators managing MCP clients and AI Trust Layer policies are affected.

changes.name: LLM region routing controls
changes.summary: LLM region routing lets you restrict which geographic regions LLM traffic is routed to, using the new Model Regions tab in AI Trust Layer policies.
changes.analysis: This likely supports compliance, residency, or risk management requirements by constraining where AI traffic is processed.
changes.impact: Organizations with geographic routing requirements for LLM traffic and administrators managing AI Trust Layer policies are affected.

changes.name: Configurable masking scope for in-flight PII guardrail
changes.summary: The in-flight PII guardrail now supports a configurable masking scope that can apply to files retrieved by agents at runtime.
changes.analysis: This adds finer control over privacy protection in AI workflows that incorporate runtime file retrieval.
changes.impact: Organizations using AI guardrails and agents that process runtime-retrieved files are affected.

Integration Service.summary: Integration Service adds a new Salesforce connector activity for file retrieval. The update focuses on expanding connector capabilities for classic Salesforce attachments.
Integration Service.overall_analysis: This is a targeted connector enhancement that likely simplifies automation scenarios needing access to files stored in the classic Salesforce Attachment object.

changes.name: Salesforce Download Attachment activity
changes.summary: A new Download Attachment activity for the Salesforce connector retrieves files from the classic Salesforce `Attachment` object.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces implementation effort for automations that need to extract legacy Salesforce attachments.
changes.impact: Developers and integration builders using the Salesforce connector with classic Attachment records are affected.

IXP.summary: IXP adds support for email transform tags in Communications Mining. The feature gives more control over how raw emails are converted into messages.
IXP.overall_analysis: This enhancement likely improves preprocessing flexibility and data quality for email-based Communications Mining use cases by allowing more deliberate transformation behavior.

changes.name: Email transform tags in Communications Mining
changes.summary: Communications Mining now supports email transform tags to control how raw emails are converted into messages, including text format, signature extraction, and default user properties.
changes.analysis: This likely helps teams tailor ingestion behavior and improve message consistency or downstream analysis quality.
changes.impact: Users configuring Communications Mining for email ingestion are affected.

Maestro.summary: Maestro introduces a new case-management project type and improves BPMN canvas usability. The release expands product scope beyond BPMN and streamlines process design.
Maestro.overall_analysis: These changes suggest Maestro is evolving into a broader orchestration and case-management platform. They likely improve both support for goal-driven work and day-to-day modeling efficiency.

changes.name: Maestro Case project type
changes.summary: Maestro Case is a new project type for goal-driven, agentic case management, complementing Maestro BPMN. It includes a Case Plan Designer, a Case Manager, a built-in Case App, and case instance management.
changes.analysis: This likely broadens Maestro to support less linear, case-oriented work where goals and evolving state matter alongside process models.
changes.impact: Teams designing case-management solutions and organizations evaluating agentic, goal-driven workflows are affected.

changes.name: Canvas fluidity updates
changes.summary: Canvas fluidity updates streamline how you build and configure BPMN processes, with a richer element toolbar, a quick add menu, and an improved Properties panel.
changes.analysis: This likely improves modeling speed and usability for BPMN authors.
changes.impact: Users building and configuring BPMN processes in Maestro are affected.

Orchestrator.summary: Orchestrator adds navigation and execution identity improvements, including a cross-folder folder shortcut, updated identity labeling and availability, tenant-level defaults, and cleanup of deleted references. The changes focus on usability and identity management.
Orchestrator.overall_analysis: The release improves administrative consistency and execution identity handling while making job navigation easier. It likely reduces configuration friction and helps standardize how jobs inherit identities across folders.

changes.name: Go to folder action in cross-folder Jobs grid
changes.summary: The cross-folder Jobs grid now includes a Go to folder inline action on each row.
changes.analysis: This likely improves navigation efficiency when reviewing jobs across multiple folders.
changes.impact: Users monitoring or managing jobs across folders are affected.

changes.name: Run as Myself relabeled and expanded
changes.summary: Run as Myself is now labeled Inherit parent job identity and is now also available for Windows (foreground) automations.
changes.analysis: This likely clarifies the feature’s behavior and extends it to more execution scenarios.
changes.impact: Users configuring job execution identities, including for Windows foreground automations, are affected.

changes.name: Tenant-level default execution identity
changes.summary: You can now configure a tenant-level default execution identity that is automatically applied to new folders as they are created.
changes.analysis: This likely promotes consistency and reduces manual setup for new folder creation.
changes.impact: Tenant administrators creating and governing folders are affected.

changes.name: Automatic cleanup of deleted user or machine references
changes.summary: References to deleted users or machines are now automatically removed from the tenant-level Default Execution Identity configuration.
changes.analysis: This likely reduces stale configuration and administrative cleanup effort.
changes.impact: Tenant administrators managing default execution identity settings are affected.

Solutions.summary: Solutions receives a redesigned deployment experience and tighter resource selection behavior. The changes aim to guide lifecycle operations and avoid inappropriate Personal Workspace resource suggestions.
Solutions.overall_analysis: These updates likely make deployments more structured and reduce configuration mistakes, especially in cross-environment lifecycle operations.

changes.name: Redesigned deployment experience
changes.summary: A redesigned deployment experience is being introduced across Studio Web and Orchestrator, with a guided, step-by-step flow for solution lifecycle operations.
changes.analysis: This likely improves deployment clarity and consistency by structuring the process into guided steps.
